Rest Now, Chief

For Jim - the man wearing many hats

The story behind it

Not a eulogy- a Celebration of Life!

For Jim, the Chief.

For thirty-nine years, when the phone rang on Southern Avenue in the middle of the night, he was out the door before it stopped ringing. Stonewood named the firehouse after him, but he always said it belonged to the town.

He married Karen near Christmastime and loved her for almost sixty-five years. Together they raised five: Jamie, Chris, Bridget, Paul, and Mark. When other families were grieving, he was the one at the door with a plate of supper and a quiet prayer.

His grandkids and great-grandkids carry a piece of him everywhere they go. The fires are out now. Rest now, Chief.

Lyrics

Verse 1
When the phone would ring on Southern Avenue
In the dead of night, somehow we always knew
He'd be gone before the ringing died
Into the night with his coat open wide
Ten coats to share and a heart to give
Thirty-nine years, that's the way he lived
They gave the firehouse his name, it's true
But he'd tell you it belonged to all of you

Chorus
Rest now, Chief, the night is still
(rest now, Chief)
We'll take the call, we always will
You gave this town your every day
Now let us carry you the rest of the way
Hang up your coat, lay your helmet down
The fires are out all over town
Rest now, Chief, it's a quiet night
(quiet night)
The first one off in your whole life

Verse 2
He married Karen near Christmastime
Near sixty-five years, still his valentine
Jamie, the steady one, calm and true
Chris, the stubborn one, through and through
They called Bridget "Hollywood," and she'd lose her cool
And Paul was "Slick," the best-dressed boy in school
And Mark, the baby, so small and dear
Five little hearts, and he held them near

Chorus
Rest now, Chief, the night is still
(rest now, Chief)
We'll take the call, we always will
You gave this town your every day
Now let us carry you the rest of the way
Hang up your coat, lay your helmet down
The fires are out all over town
Rest now, Chief, it's a quiet night
(quiet night)
The first one off in your whole life

Bridge
When others grieved, he'd be standing there
With a plate of supper and a quiet prayer
Now the ones he fed have gathered too
To set a place at the table for you

Final Chorus
Rest now, Chief, the night is still
(rest now, Chief)
We'll take the call, we always will
You gave this town your every day
Now let us carry you the rest of the way
Hang up your coat, lay your helmet down
Your name still shines in Stonewood town
Rest now, Chief, it's a quiet night
(quiet night)
Your family's keeping watch tonight

Outro
Somewhere a Mustang's rolling slow
Under the stars, where the good ones go
And all his grandkids, and their little ones too
Every one of them a piece of you
(rest now, Chief)
